255.sense: Ayat al-Kursi is one sentence of theology said without a single pause for objection. It denies Allah a partner, then sleep, then any intercessor who has not been permitted, then any limit on His knowledge, then any strain in holding all of it. Each clause closes a door that human beings habitually leave open when they imagine God.

notes.t: The Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy ibn Kaʿb which verse of the Book of Allah was the greatest. Ubayy answered with this one, and the Prophet ﷺ struck him on the chest and said: may knowledge be pleasant for you, Abu al-Mundhir.

Abu Hurayra was told by a thief he caught at night: when you go to your bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi, and a guardian from Allah will remain over you and no devil will come near you until morning. The Prophet ﷺ confirmed it, and added that the thief had been Satan, and had told the truth while being a habitual liar.
Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him is not a small remark. Sleep is the daily proof that a living thing is not self-sufficient. Denying it denies the whole category of need.

What the Kursi is has more than one answer from the earliest generations. Reports from Ibn Abbas describe it as the place of the two Feet, distinct from the Throne; another report from him reads it as His knowledge. The scholars did not agree, and the honest position is that the word is affirmed and its manner is not known.
notes.src: reports from Ibn ʿAbbās point both ways; at-Tabari lists them without deciding

notes.t: They encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. The verse concedes that human beings do know things, and then names the only reason they do.

links.why: the verse immediately after, on compulsion in religion, is read by many as its consequence
